 Critic's Review User Reviews Tum Mere Ho Movie Review: Gurmeet Choudhary Brings Heart to an Intensely Familiar Love Story 
 Ronak Kotecha Oct 22, 2026, 6:30 PM IST 3.0 /5 
 Story: Tum Mere Ho follows Akash ( Gurmeet Choudhary ) and Tamanna ( Isha Malviya ), whose love seems doomed from the start. As they navigate unexpected challenges, emotional turmoil and difficult choices, will their love triumph against all odds, or is a happy ending not meant for them? Review: One-sided love stories can be very interesting. By their very nature, they can have some rather unexpected consequences. The possibilities range from thrill and obsession to, in some cases, self-destruction. Director and co-writer Ashish Panda , along with Shanwaz Kader Khan , crafts a fairly interesting story around this subject, with a touch of unpredictability in the way its characters behave. Akash is a daredevil who believes life is meant to be lived on the edge. Flying is his passion, but when he meets Tamanna, he finds himself falling in love all over again. However, this love story isn’t nearly as straightforward as it initially seems. Tamanna’s chirpy demeanour and nonchalant attitude towards life could be a false exterior to a deeply disturbing truth about her. To say that the film has a Saiyaara hangover wouldn’t be a stretch. But then again, most intense love stories need pain at their core, and in that sense, Tum Mere Ho is no different. However, the film’s execution has a certain freshness that keeps it novel for the most part. Gurmeet Choudhary looks dreamy, with his chiselled looks and washboard abs. Heck, he looks more beautiful than the heroine, and one cannot quite fathom how a guy like him could be a victim of one-sided love. Jokes aside, the actor, who is also the co-producer alongside his wife, Debina Bonnerjee, puts his all into making his character work. But we’ve seen these tropes so many times before that, for an actor, the biggest challenge in playing a lovelorn, obsessive lover is finding a way to make the character feel different. Gurmeet succeeds in making Akash likeable despite some of his obviously problematic traits. Debutante Isha Malviya is good for her first film. Her girl-next-door looks work for the role, and she gets enough scope to showcase her range. However, her performance could benefit from fewer clichés and a little more conviction. At times, she comes across as a tad stiff, and a more natural approach could have made her character more convincing. Shaan R Grover as Sahil does well in his limited screen time. The film’s soundtrack is a major saving grace. When the story wobbles, the music redeems what unfolds on screen. The music, composed by Mithoon and a battery of other composers, is beautifully filmed and adds to the film’s emotional appeal. The title track, Tum Mere Ho , is the best of the lot, while Winter Ayun Waliye 2.0 stands out as a fun number, thanks to its delightful banter. The dialogues are relatable, too, helping the film connect with its audience even when the narrative loses some of its grip. Overall, Tum Mere Ho adds itself to the season’s roster of intense love stories and has its moments of love, pain and longing. Whether it has that elusive X-factor to become the next cult love story is something only time will tell. Videos
